paper: Hu et al. 2019, Infect Drug Resist 12:1285-1288 (pPA1011, MH734334.1)

open_questions.q: Is the pPA1011 backbone truly novel across the full corpus of Pseudomonas aeruginosa blaKPC-carrying plasmids, or is it best described as a p14057-family variant?
open_questions.basis: This replication compared pPA1011 (MH734334.1) against only ONE prior comparator (p14057, KY296095.1) and already recovered 51,587 / 62,793 bp = 82.15% of pPA1011 at 98.70% weighted identity. The paper's 'novel plasmid backbone' claim is only weakly supported by that single comparator; the true novelty rank across all P. aeruginosa KPC plasmids in NCBI (and against Enterobacterales KPC plasmids that may share IncP-6 / IncN / IncU backbone modules) is unknown.
next_steps: BLAST pPA1011 against all NCBI nucleotide entries filtered by organism=Pseudomonas aeruginosa AND 'plasmid' AND blaKPC, take the top matching backbone by union coverage.
Independently run PlasmidFinder / Mash-screen against a curated plasmid database (e.g., PLSDB) to assign an incompatibility group / plasmid family and report the closest known relative by ANI.

Report the 'unique to pPA1011' ~11.2 kb (~18%) segment coordinates and BLAST that fragment separately against nr to check whether it is a truly novel insertion or a mobilized module from a known source.

open_questions.q: Are the ORFs annotated as 'hypothetical protein' immediately flanking blaKPC-2 in MH734334.1 in fact ISKpn8 (upstream) and ISKpn6 / IS26 (downstream), as the paper's schematic implies?
open_questions.basis: The paper diagrams the blaKPC-2 context as ΔIS6-Tn3-ISKpn8-blaKPC-2-ISKpn6-IS26. In the deposited GenBank record, the CDSs at the ISKpn8 and ISKpn6/IS26 positions are annotated generically as 'hypothetical protein', so this replication could only confirm coordinate-consistency, not IS-family identity. The paper's central novelty claim (novel IS-mediated context) rests on those IS-family calls.
next_steps: Extract the CDS nucleotide + protein sequences at positions 16,420-17,400 (putative ISKpn8) and 18,807-20,289 (putative ISKpn6 / IS26) from MH734334.1.
Submit those sequences to ISfinder (https://isfinder.biotoul.fr) and also run ISEScan on the whole plasmid; record IS-family, group, inverted-repeat coordinates, and target-site duplications.
Compare the identified IS elements against the exact IS-family strings named in the paper's schema and flag any mismatch (e.g., ISKpn18 vs ISKpn8, IS26 vs IS15DIV).

open_questions.q: Is pPA1011 self-transmissible by conjugation, or is it a mobilizable / non-transmissible plasmid that requires a helper?
open_questions.basis: The paper reports the plasmid sequence and its blaKPC-2 context but its clinical significance depends on horizontal-transfer potential. MH734334.1 encodes KlcA (annotated at 20,417-20,842) which is a plasmid-partitioning / stability protein, but the presence and completeness of a Type-IV secretion system (tra / trb / virB) and an origin of transfer (oriT) is not addressed by this replication. In P. aeruginosa, KPC dissemination is dominated by mobilizable rather than fully conjugative plasmids, and this matters for infection-control planning.
next_steps: Run oriTfinder (https://tool-mml.sjtu.edu.cn/oriTfinder/) on MH734334.1 to detect oriT, relaxase, T4CP, and T4SS gene clusters.
Cross-check with MOB-suite / MOB-typer to classify pPA1011 as conjugative, mobilizable, or non-mobilizable and to assign a MOB (relaxase) family.

If a wet-lab collaborator is available, attempt filter-mating with a rifampin-resistant P. aeruginosa PAO1 recipient and select on meropenem + rifampin to measure conjugation frequency; a negative result under helper-free conditions would classify pPA1011 as mobilizable-only.

open_questions.q: Does the sequenced clinical isolate PA1011 carry additional resistance determinants (chromosomal or on other plasmids) that co-explain the reported carbapenem resistance phenotype, beyond plasmid-borne blaKPC-2?
open_questions.basis: Only the plasmid MH734334.1 was deposited; the chromosomal WGS of PA1011 is not accessible under this study on SRA. P. aeruginosa carbapenem resistance is frequently multi-factorial (OprD porin loss, AmpC overexpression, chromosomal blaVIM/IMP MBLs, efflux upregulation). Attributing the isolate's meropenem/imipenem MICs solely to plasmid blaKPC-2 without the chromosomal context is premature.
next_steps: Search NCBI BioSample / BioProject linked to the MH734334.1 submitter (Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University) for a matching PA1011 WGS deposit under a related study accession.

If a WGS exists, run ResFinder / CARD-RGI on the chromosomal assembly and specifically check OprD (loss-of-function mutations), ampC / ampD / ampR (derepression alleles), mexAB-oprM / mexXY regulators, and any additional carbapenemases.

If no WGS exists, note this as an irreducible provenance gap and recommend the isolate be re-sequenced (short + long reads) and re-deposited with full chromosomal + plasmid replicons linked in one BioProject.

open_questions.q: Is the ST463 MLST call for PA1011 correct, and how does the ST463 lineage relate to the known geographic and temporal distribution of KPC-2-producing P. aeruginosa in China?
open_questions.basis: This replication accepted the ST463 designation from the /note='genotype: ST463' qualifier on the MH734334.1 LOCUS metadata, which is submitter-provided and not independently re-typed. ST463 has since been reported as an emerging KPC-2-producing P. aeruginosa high-risk clone in China; whether PA1011 is an early representative of that clonal expansion or a sporadic ST463 case is a substantive open epidemiological question that cannot be answered without the isolate WGS.
next_steps: Obtain the PA1011 WGS (see Q4) and run mlst (Torsten Seemann) against the PubMLST P. aeruginosa scheme to independently confirm ST463.
Build a core-genome SNP tree of PA1011 against all publicly available ST463 P. aeruginosa genomes (Enterobase / NCBI Pathogen Detection) and date its position within the ST463 clonal expansion.

Cross-reference the collection date (2019 report; isolate presumably 2017-2018) with published ST463 KPC-2 surveillance in China to place PA1011 chronologically within the ST463 KPC-2 emergence timeline.
